source: Ye, Chen, Dillig, Durrett (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting
finding: The LLM writes a declarative spec (constraints) and an SMT/SAT solver (Z3) finds the answer. This beat the same model writing an imperative program (PAL) and chain of thought on constraint-style tasks.
numbers: code-davinci-002, greedy. GSM-SYS: SATLM 69.4 vs PROGLM 43.4, CoT 46.5, standard 21.0. ALGEBRA 77.5 vs 52.3. LSAT 35.0 vs CoT 23.5. BoardgameQA 79.4 vs CoT 60.7. CLUTRR 68.3 vs PROGLM 58.9. ProofWriter depth-5 99.7 vs 83.7. Plain GSM: 71.8 vs PROGLM 72.7 (on par). Abstract: +23% over PAL on a hard GSM subset.
limits: Table columns were read from a PDF text dump; row order checked against the paper text. Gains vanish where the task is plain forward arithmetic. Code-davinci-002 is a retired model.
agent_relevance: Supports S4/S7: have the model state constraints, let code check or solve. Declarative beats imperative when the task needs search.

source: Ye, Chen, Dillig, Durrett (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting (ablations)
finding: Removing the solver and asking the model to answer directly gives only standard-prompt accuracy. Keeping the declarative step but solving with CoT recovers part of the gain. The solver gives the rest.
numbers: SATCOTSOLVER beats CoT by 7.9 points on GSM-SYS and 8.1 on CLUTRR. SATNOSOLVER is on par with STANDARD.
limits: Two datasets of three shown in the ablation table.
agent_relevance: Two separate gains: better parsing format, and a sound solver. Our scaffold should keep both: restate as constraints, then run code.

source: Ye, Chen, Dillig, Durrett (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting (error split)
finding: When CoT-as-solver fails, many errors are planning errors, which a real solver removes.
numbers: Planning errors vs execution errors of COTSOLVER: GSM-SYS 72.5% vs 27.5%; GSM 42.5% vs 57.5%; CLUTRR 47.5% vs 52.5%.
limits: Small hand-labelled samples (about 40 errors per set).
agent_relevance: Search and planning are where plain model reasoning breaks. Offload them.

source: Ye, Chen, Dillig, Durrett (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting (parsing confidence)
finding: Declarative output is not always easier for the model to write. Token log likelihood is higher for the SAT form on two of three sets.
numbers: Log likelihood (unnormalised) SAT vs PAL: GSM-SYS -8.5 vs -9.5; CLUTRR -2.0 vs -3.1; GSM -9.7 vs -9.2 (PAL higher).
limits: Log likelihood is a rough proxy for ease of parsing.
agent_relevance: Do not assume declarative always wins. Test per task type.

source: Pan, Albalak, Wang, Wang (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
finding: LLM translates to a symbolic form, then Pyke (rules), Prover9 (FOL), python-constraint (CSP) or Z3 (SAT, used for AR-LSAT) solves. A self-refine step uses solver error messages.
numbers: GPT-4 accuracy Standard/CoT/Logic-LM: PrOntoQA 77.4/98.8/83.2; ProofWriter 52.7/68.1/79.7; FOLIO 69.1/70.6/78.9; LogicalDeduction 71.3/75.3/87.6; AR-LSAT 33.3/35.1/43.0.
limits: On PrOntoQA with GPT-4, CoT (98.8) beats Logic-LM (83.2). Falls back to CoT when the formula does not run. Test sets small for AR-LSAT.
agent_relevance: Solver help is largest on search-like tasks (AR-LSAT, LogicalDeduction), not on simple forward chaining.

source: Pan, Albalak, Wang, Wang (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning (averages)
finding: Average gains over standard and CoT prompting; CoT hurts on search-like tasks.
numbers: GPT-3.5: +39.2% over standard, +18.4% over CoT. GPT-4: +24.98% over standard, +10.44% over CoT. CoT gain on AR-LSAT: -3.2%; FOLIO +11.75%; PrOntoQA +51.59%.
limits: Average over five datasets with different baselines.
agent_relevance: CoT is the wrong tool for constraint tasks; route them to a solver.

source: Pan, Albalak, Wang, Wang (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning (executability)
finding: The bottleneck is writing a formula that runs. Self-refinement from solver error text raises the share that runs, mostly on hard sets.
numbers: Executable rate before to after self-refine, GPT-3.5 / GPT-4: AR-LSAT 11.3%->21.8% / 32.6%->39.8%; FOLIO 66.7%->84.3% / 79.9%->85.8%; ProofWriter 87.3%->95.6% (GPT-3.5). When AR-LSAT formulas do run, accuracy is 57.7 (GPT-3.5) and 60.0 (GPT-4). Average rate gain from refinement 5.01 points.
limits: Accuracy on executable cases is selected (easier cases run). Refinement gave no gain on FOLIO accuracy for GPT-4 (80.4 to 79.9).
agent_relevance: Budget retries on the formalisation step. Feed the solver error back (guardrail G2: revise from real output).

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Logical Reasoning by Combining Language Models with First-Order Logic Provers
finding: LLM translates to first-order logic, Prover9 decides, 10-way majority vote over translations. Big gain on ProofWriter, none on FOLIO for GPT-4.
numbers: ProofWriter (balanced subset, 120 per label): LINC 96.4% (GPT-3.5) and 98.3% (GPT-4). StarCoder+ (15.5B) with LINC beats GPT-3.5 CoT by 38 points and GPT-4 CoT by 10 points.
limits: ProofWriter is synthetic with short sentences. Authors suggest this favours formalisation.
agent_relevance: A small model plus a prover can beat a big model alone on deduction. Check the task is formalisable first.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Logical Reasoning by Combining Language Models with First-Order Logic Provers (FOLIO)
finding: On human-written FOLIO, GPT-4 with LINC did not beat CoT. The gap was not significant.
numbers: GPT-4 LINC vs CoT on FOLIO: McNemar p = 0.58. StarCoder+ and GPT-3.5 improved with LINC.
limits: FOLIO has about 5.3 premises per item, ProofWriter 18.8. Natural text loses information in translation.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: gains shrink when the language is messy and the translation loses meaning.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Logical Reasoning by Combining Language Models with First-Order Logic Provers (error analysis)
finding: Translation errors dominate LINC failures. Syntax errors in the formulas are common, and missing implicit premises give false Uncertain.
numbers: Syntax error rate in generated FOL: 38% StarCoder+, 24% GPT-3.5, 13% GPT-4. Commonest: one symbol used with different arities. Another mode: implicit facts (e.g. Person(Harry)) not encoded.
limits: Count over all generations, not only wrong answers.
agent_relevance: Run a cheap syntax and arity check in code before calling the solver. Add background facts explicitly.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Logical Reasoning by Combining Language Models with First-Order Logic Provers (proof depth)
finding: CoT collapses on deep proofs; the prover does not.
numbers: GPT-3.5 baselines near chance beyond proof depth 1; GPT-3.5 with LINC near perfect at all depths. GPT-4 with LINC near ceiling at max depth.
limits: Read from figures; exact per-depth values not recorded.
agent_relevance: Depth and many irrelevant premises hurt model reasoning, not solver reasoning.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Logical Reasoning by Combining Language Models with First-Order Logic Provers (complementarity)
finding: CoT and LINC succeed about equally often on FOLIO but on different items, so failure modes differ.
numbers: Authors report distinct and complementary failure modes (three for each method).
limits: Qualitative sample analysis.
agent_relevance: Supports G4: combine unlike methods, not same-model samples.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas
finding: 2100 puzzles built from CNF formulas (4 to 50 clauses, avg 36 variables), checked with a solver. Models must say SAT/UNSAT and give an assignment or an unsat core.
numbers: Zero-shot accuracy: o4-mini 89.3 avg; DeepSeek-R1 87.8; DeepSeek-V3 84.0; Claude-3.7-Sonnet 74.8; gpt-4o 58.0; Llama-3.1-8B 38.2. Hard (31-50 clauses): o4-mini 78.0, R1 78.6, average over all models 53.0 (chance 50).
limits: Stories written by an LLM; some noise despite validation.
agent_relevance: Models without tools barely beat coin flips on hard satisfiability. A real solver call is the fix.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas (SAT vs UNSAT)
finding: Models do much worse on UNSAT than SAT. Proving no model exists is the hard direction.
numbers: Averages on hard: SAT 66.7%, UNSAT 39.3%. Hard UNSAT: gpt-4o 18.9, gpt-4o-mini 13.2, Llama-4-Maverick 17.9, o4-mini 65.0, R1 83.6, V3 74.3.
limits: Many UNSAT figures sit below the 50% chance line: those models say SAT too often.
agent_relevance: Never trust a model's 'consistent' verdict. The consistency check must be code (G3, G5).

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas (scaling)
finding: Bigger models inside a family do not fix hard instances.
numbers: Hard-instance accuracy plateaus near 50-53% for Qwen3, Llama-3.1, Llama-4 and DeepSeek-Distill families at the largest sizes.
limits: Reasoning-tuned models (o4-mini, R1) escape the plateau partly.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on model size for search; use test-time compute or a solver.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas (error types)
finding: Main error types: satisfiability bias (claim SAT, give an invalid assignment), context inconsistency, condition omission.
numbers: o4-mini: satisfiability bias 68.7%, context inconsistency 17.0%, condition omission 14.3%. DeepSeek-R1: 40.5%, 44.7%, 12.6%.
limits: Qualitative classification of wrong predictions.
agent_relevance: Verify any proposed assignment by plugging it into every clause in code. That catches the top error.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas (trace correctness)
finding: A right label often comes with an invalid reasoning trace.
numbers: Prediction vs trace accuracy: o4-mini 94.7 SAT prediction, 74.4 overall trace; DeepSeek-R1 85.2 SAT prediction, 78.0 overall trace; Claude-3.7 54.2 trace; DeepSeek-V3 68.4 trace.
limits: Trace judged against the unsat core or assignment.
agent_relevance: Written reasoning is not a record of correct checking. Grade the assignment, not the story.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning
finding: Logic grid puzzles from CSPs with controlled size. Difficulty measured by search space and by Z3 conflict count. Accuracy falls sharply with size: the curse of complexity.
numbers: Grid-level accuracy: o1-full 81.0, DeepSeek-R1 78.7, o1-preview 71.4, o1-mini 59.7, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 36.2, Llama-3.1-405B 32.6. X-large puzzles: o1-full 42.5, R1 28.5, o1-preview 17.0, Llama-405B 0.0. Most non-reasoning models near zero beyond about 10^7 search space.
limits: Puzzles assume a unique solution exists.
agent_relevance: Z3 conflicts is a usable difficulty gauge. Hard cases need search, not recall.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning (sampling)
finding: With an oracle that picks the right sample, GPT-4o sampling nearly matches o1. Without the oracle, majority vote helps little. The gap is a selection problem.
numbers: GPT-4o base 31.7. Best-of-N oracle: N=32 60.3, N=128 69.1. Majority vote N=32: 38.0 (more samples did not help). Self-verify prompts gave small or no gains without an oracle.
limits: Reward model result in the table could not be read cleanly and is not recorded.
agent_relevance: A solver or checker is the missing selector. Code checks, not votes (G5).

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning (reasoning tokens)
finding: o1 spends about ten times more hidden reasoning tokens than GPT-4o, and token count tracks Z3 conflicts until a plateau.
numbers: Mean hidden tokens: o1-mini 5,145; o1-preview 5,346 vs GPT-4o-mini 503; GPT-4o 544. About 400 tokens per Z3 conflict below 20 conflicts; plateau above 30 conflicts. Wrong answers use more tokens than right ones.
limits: Hidden token counts were from API usage figures.
agent_relevance: Search effort the model cannot extend is exactly where an external solver should take over.

source: Hao, Chen, Zhang, Fan (2025) Large Language Models Can Solve Real-World Planning Rigorously with Formal Verification Tools
finding: LLM turns a travel query into Z3 SMT code; the solver finds a plan. Final pass rate on TravelPlanner jumped.
numbers: TravelPlanner final pass: validation 180 queries: GPT-4 direct 4.4, o1-preview direct 10.0, ours Claude-3 93.3, GPT-4 93.3, Mistral-Large 66.7. Test 1000 queries: Claude-3 93.9, GPT-4 90.2, Mistral-Large 67.8, GPT-4 direct 4.4.
limits: Weaker model (Mistral-Large) loses on delivery rate (72.2%) because its code does not run. Prompts were tuned on training queries.
agent_relevance: Strongest recent case for the S4/S7 pattern: model writes constraints, SMT solver decides.

source: Hao, Chen, Zhang, Fan (2025) Large Language Models Can Solve Real-World Planning Rigorously with Formal Verification Tools (generalisation)
finding: Same framework, zero-shot, on four other combinatorial tasks: far more optimal solutions than a two-stage LLM planner.
numbers: Optimal rate, ours (GPT-4o) vs TwoStage (GPT-4o): block picking 92 vs 4; task allocation 92 vs 0; TSP 100 vs 0; warehouse 72 vs 0.
limits: Small synthetic task sets.
agent_relevance: Constraint encoding transfers across tasks without new training.

source: Hao, Chen, Zhang, Fan (2025) Large Language Models Can Solve Real-World Planning Rigorously with Formal Verification Tools (unsat queries)
finding: When the query is infeasible, the Z3 unsat core is turned into a reason and a modification suggestion.
numbers: Repairs and solves on average 81.6% and 91.7% of unsatisfiable queries from two datasets (more iterations allowed in the second).
limits: Simulated user preferences.
agent_relevance: The unsat core is the exact real failing output that G2 asks revisions to cite.

source: Wu, Barrett, Narodytska (2024) Lemur: Integrating LLMs in Automated Program Verification
finding: LLM proposes loop invariants; an automated reasoner (ESBMC, Ultimate Automizer, SMT-based) checks them. Calculus proved sound.
numbers: Code2Inv 133 programs: ESBMC 68, Code2Inv 92, Lemur-GPT-3.5 103, Lemur-GPT-4 107 (avg 4.7 proposals; one needed 90). SV-COMP 47 hard programs, 15 min: Lemur-GPT-4 25, Lemur-GPT-3.5 14, ESBMC 1, UAutomizer 1.
limits: Benchmarks under 150 tokens.
agent_relevance: Propose with the model, verify by solver, loop on failure. A direct template for S4/S7.

source: Lyu et al. (2023) Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Translate to a symbolic chain, run a deterministic solver (Python or Datalog). Beats CoT on 9 of 10 benchmarks.
numbers: Relative gain: math word problems 6.3%, planning 3.4%, multi-hop QA 5.5%, relational inference (CLUTRR) 21.4%; GSM8K +14% (greedy). No gain on Sports; far below baselines on StrategyQA.
limits: Not an SMT solver, but same pattern. Codex model. Fails where difficulty is knowledge, not reasoning.
agent_relevance: Choose solver offload by task type: no gain when facts, not logic, are the hard part.

source: Xia et al. (2024) Fuzz4All: Universal Fuzzing with Large Language Models
finding: Reverse direction: an LLM generates SMT2 test inputs to find bugs in SMT solvers (Z3, CVC5).
numbers: 98 bugs found across 9 systems, 64 confirmed new. Z3: 14 reported; CVC5: 9 reported. Average coverage gain over prior best fuzzers +36.8% across 6 languages. Input is valid if the SMT solver returns SAT or UNSAT.
limits: Share of valid LLM-made inputs is often low (about 37-50% on several targets).
agent_relevance: Solvers can be wrong. Do not treat a solver verdict as ground truth without a second check.

source: Feng et al. (2023) Language Models can be Logical Solvers (LoGiPT)
finding: Fine-tunes a 13B model to imitate the solver's reasoning, so a parse error no longer means no answer.
numbers: ProofWriter / PrOntoQA: LoGiPT Vicuna-13B 81.17/96.40; CodeLlama-13B 89.50/95.60; Logic-LM GPT-4 79.66/83.20; GPT-4 CoT 68.11/98.79.
limits: Imitated solver has no soundness guarantee. Needs training, which we do not do.
agent_relevance: Shows the failure mode of parse errors; our fix is retry and syntax checks, not training.

source: Kirtania, Gupta, Radhakrishna (2024) Logic-LM++: Multi-Step Refinement for Symbolic Formulations
finding: Refinement can make formulas worse. A backtracking agent compares the new version with the old by pairwise comparison and reverts if worse.
numbers: Average +5% over Logic-LM, +18.5% over standard, +12.3% over CoT on FOLIO, ProofWriter, AR-LSAT. Backtracking raises execution accuracy about 6% (GPT-4) and 3% (GPT-3.5); execution rate gain under 1%.
limits: LLM judges the two versions. Example error: 'No young person teaches' became 'All young people teach'.
agent_relevance: Refine only from solver output, keep the old version, and compare by code on held-out cases (G2, G3, G5).

source: Ganguly et al. (2024) Proof of Thought: Neurosymbolic Program Synthesis allows Robust and Interpretable Reasoning
finding: JSON DSL compiled to Z3 first-order logic. Feedback loop of 3 steps. Weak on open-ended commonsense.
numbers: StrategyQA, 1000 questions: 82.4% compiled; recall 91.40%, precision 58.22%, F1 71.13%, false positive rate 53.98%.
limits: Overpredicts yes; 17.6% fail to compile. Small domain-specific demo.
agent_relevance: Z3 proves what was encoded, not what is true. Encoding errors give confident wrong answers.

source: Arakelyan et al. (2025) FLARE: Faithful Logic-Aided Reasoning and Exploration
finding: Model writes a logic program and simulates the search itself with no external solver. Handles fuzzy questions solvers cannot.
numbers: SOTA on 7 of 9 reasoning and 3 of 3 logic sets. Successful traces show 18.1% more unique emergent facts and 8.6% higher overlap between code relations and the execution trace.
limits: Simulated search is not sound.
agent_relevance: Pair soft simulated reasoning with a real check when a hard answer is needed.

source: Michailidis, Tsouros, Guns (2026) DCP-Bench-Open: Evaluating LLMs for Constraint Modelling of Discrete Combinatorial Problems
finding: 164 problems; LLMs write constraint models in MiniZinc, CPMpy, OR-Tools; solution-level accuracy. Python frameworks do better.
numbers: Zero-shot best: Python frameworks up to 75% vs 57.3% MiniZinc (Qwen3-Coder). OR-Tools: gpt-oss-120b 75.0, gpt-5.1 71.3. With prompting plus inference-time compute (including self-verification) up to 91%.
limits: Tested model list changes fast.
agent_relevance: Use a high-level, widely seen modelling API (Python). Self-verify with solver traceback.

source: de Moura and Bjorner (2008) Z3: An Efficient SMT Solver
finding: Standard SMT solver used in SATLM, Logic-LM, ZebraLogic and Hao et al. Not opened; named here as the common backend.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: Use Z3 through its Python API from the code layer.

source: Mitchell, Selman, Levesque (1992) Hard and easy distributions of SAT problems
finding: Background from memory: random 3-SAT is hardest near a clause-to-variable ratio of about 4.26, in line with the SATBench and ZebraLogic finding that model accuracy falls with problem size. Not opened.
numbers: Not read.
limits: From memory, not verified this session.
agent_relevance: Difficulty can be tuned by clause ratio.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLM-Modulo (as cited in Hao et al.)
finding: As reported in the Hao et al. introduction: LLM plus external critics raised TravelPlanner pass rate to 20% (GPT-4-Turbo) and 65% (o1-preview). Original paper not opened.
numbers: 20% and 65% as quoted.
limits: Secondhand number.
agent_relevance: Same loop shape: propose, critique with code, retry.
